title: Himeji Castle
summary: Himeji Castle stands on a hill in the Harima Plain, Hyogo Prefecture. Toyotomi Hideyoshi built a first castle there in 1581, and the daimyo Ikeda Terumasa remodelled it between 1601 and 1609 into largely the form seen today. UNESCO calls it the finest surviving early 17th-century Japanese castle, with 82 buildings. Its wooden keep is 31.5 m tall, and one source says the castle was never attacked.

uncertainty.note: 1601-1609 is Ikeda Terumasa's remodelling, which World History Encyclopedia says produced largely the present form; the first castle dates from 1581 and the same source gives the whole build as 1581-1609.

as_recorded.value: remodelled between 1601 and 1609 CE by the daimyo or feudal lord, Ikeda Terumasa
